root_cause.text: Multiple kthread exit paths (make_task_dead(), direct do_exit(), and kthread_exit()) bypassed the affinity_node cleanup in kthread_exit(), leaving the node linked in the global kthread_affinity_list while the kthread struct was freed and reused, causing memory corruption when another kthread's list_del() wrote through dangling pointers into the reallocated memory.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description explicitly states: "When a kthread exits via make_task_dead() it bypasses kthread_exit() and misses the affinity_node cleanup. free_kthread_struct() frees the memory while the node is still linked into the global kthread_affinity_list. A subsequent list_del() by another kthread writes through dangling list pointers into the freed and reused memory, corrupting the pid's rcu.func pointer." The patch consolidates all exit paths by converting kthread_exit() to a macro that calls do_exit(), and adding kthread_do_exit() which is invoked from do_exit() for any task with PF_KTHREAD set, ensuring cleanup always occurs regardless of which exit path is taken.
